title: Return-to-YTIntel crash fixed
summary: YTIntel now survives leaving the site and returning through browser Back/Forward without collapsing into the blank black shell shown in the reported screenshot. YouTube links are hardened to open in a separate tab, and a lifecycle recovery guard restores the app shell, active view and visibility state on BFCache/history returns, focus and visibility restoration.
discord_changes: 🐛 RETURN CRASH FIXED: leaving YTIntel for YouTube and coming back can no longer leave the app as a blank black page.
↩️ BFCache / HISTORY RECOVERY: pageshow, popstate, focus and visibility-return guards restore the shell, remove stale loading/prehide state and ensure an active view exists.
🔗 YOUTUBE LINKS STAY SAFE: YouTube links generated inside YTIntel are forced into a separate tab with noopener/noreferrer so research does not replace the working YTIntel tab.
🧪 NEW PRODUCTION PROOF: a dedicated live browser test now deliberately hides the shell, fires a BFCache-style return, navigates away and comes back, then verifies YTIntel is still visible and usable.
changes: Added v378-navigation-resilience.js as a final lifecycle guard after the existing Analyse, Creator Assets, resumable upload and Scene Index modules load.
The navigation guard hardens existing and dynamically-created YouTube anchors to target a new tab and applies rel=noopener noreferrer.
Added shell restoration on pageshow (including persisted BFCache returns), popstate, window focus and visibilitychange back to visible.
Shell restoration removes stale hidden/v360-prehide/v360-loading state, removes a stale boot overlay and restores an active Analyse/Vault/Watchtower view if history restoration lost it.
Added production-v378-navigation.mjs to reproduce the reported failure class and prove recovery against the real GitHub Pages deployment.
Added a dedicated parallel navigation-return smoke job so this regression is checked quickly instead of waiting for the full video analysis smoke.
Updated the main Analyse and shell production tests to require the v0.37.8 release and the navigation resilience module.
Updated service-worker shell versioning and query cache-busters so browsers do not keep the pre-hotfix entry shell.
Updated Core CI and Pages release validation to enforce the new lifecycle guard and navigation test.
known_limitations: A literal @aaron is included in the Discord message. Discord webhooks require Aaron's numeric Discord user ID in <@USER_ID> form for a guaranteed push mention; that ID is not currently stored in YTIntel.
The lifecycle guard protects the YTIntel shell and YouTube navigation path. Browser extensions or a full renderer/browser process crash remain outside the app's control.
Automatic Scene Index remains sampled rather than frame-by-frame and virtual timestamp ranges are not yet physically transcoded standalone clips.
Actual Creator Assets upload capacity remains governed by the Supabase project's Storage limits and publisher/platform rights still govern footage redistribution.
why_it_matters: Research software cannot be trusted if clicking into a source video destroys the workspace on return. This hotfix turns that exact reported failure into a permanent regression test and makes the normal research loop — YTIntel → YouTube source → Back to YTIntel — resilient by design.
